t: The Argentine Confederation was defeated in the Platine War by an alliance consisting of Brazil, Uruguay and the Argentine provinces of Entre Ríos and Corrientes.
The Hospital for Sick Children, the first hospital in England to provide in-patient beds specifically for children, was founded in London.
Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel Uncle Tom's Cabin, which had a profound effect on attitudes toward African Americans and slavery in the United States, was published.
Swedish operatic soprano Jenny Lind concluded a successful concert tour of the United States under the management of showman P. T. Barnum.
The University of Sydney, Australia's oldest university, was inaugurated two years after being established by the University of Sydney Act.
A massive earthquake struck the Dutch East Indies, creating a tsunami that washed away villages, ships and residents.
Led by George Cathcart, British troops defeated Basuto and Taung forces at the Battle of Berea in present-day Lesotho, leading to an offer of peace from King Moshoeshoe I.
